correctness.rationale: With r=k+1 fixed path vertices, the forest-completion count is r n^(n−r−1), since the relevant complete-graph minor is nI−J with a single eigenvalue r; the empty minor at r=n gives 1. For a specified off-path leaf, deletion preserves the root set and gives n−1 attachments; for a marked leaf, deletion removes an isolated root. The resulting probabilities are q^(n−r−1) and (r−1)q^(n−r−1)/r (q=(n−1)/n), respectively, and the internal vertices are excluded. At r=n the formula evaluates to 2, as required for a spanning path. The fixed-path mean depends only on its length. Subtracting consecutive expressions gives the stated increment with sign of 2(n−1)−k(k+1)². This cubic is strictly increasing; the first transition is positive and the last difference is (3−n)/(n−1) when n≥4, with just a two-point tie at n=3. The integer equality gives exactly the claimed two-point plateaus; the index crossing of a monic cubic at 2(n−1) gives the cube-root asymptotic for either maximizing distance. An individual endpoint's probability strictly increases because both k/(k+1) and q^(n−k−2) increase. The uploaded finite Prüfer check was inspected, not executed, and is not required for the proof.

evidence: The 10/26 Finding gives the conditional joint law of endpoint and off-path leaves and explicitly labels the identical mean already known. Bousquet-Mélou–Chapuy count by height and in-degree in the rooted Cayley specialization; Berzunza Ojeda–Janson use distance profiles and a leaf-biased law.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Adding the two populations in the joint law recovers the global count and its mean. The profile census jointly determines total leaves (with a root correction) and the number H_k at depth k of a fixed root, so exchangeability recovers the conditional mean via E[L H_k]/E[H_k]; the inspected profile text does not explicitly simplify this ratio to the cubic rule. The leaf-biased/asymptotic paper is not in itself direct statement-level evidence of the exact formula.

originality.rationale: Two distinct records already in the Resultary corpus state this exact global mean, increment/sign criterion, complete tie rule and cube-root mode in the same uniform unrooted labeled-tree model with two fixed marked vertices. The 10/13 record also uses the same path-conditioned matrix-tree/deletion proof, and the 10/18 record gives the increment in exactly the claimed range and normalization. The marked-endpoint contrast uses the prior endpoint law. This is demonstrable equivalent coverage, not an inference of immutable posting priority from catalog dates or a failure based on searches unavailable.
